move: multiply ink plates slam in, letters stamp up, cyan ghost misregisters
how: On a paper-coloured ground three large multiply-blended discs (pink, cyan, yellow) plus two stacked uppercase words 'PRESS RUN' in dark ink with a second cyan copy of the same words underneath as a misregistered ghost plate; a fractalNoise SVG-filter grain layer sits on top at 35% opacity. In the first 30% the discs slide in with expo.out from left, right and top (x -900, x 900, y -700), then drift a few dozen pixels with sine.inOut until 83%. From 12% the letters rise from yPercent 110 with expo.out and a 0.05s stagger, the ghost plate 0.07s later, then the ghost slides from x 14 / y -8 to x -10 / y 8 so the registration wanders. The grain layer creeps x 40 / y -30 linearly. From 82% the letters shoot up to yPercent -120 (expo.in) and the discs exit the way they came, ending on bare paper.
adapt: Change the two words (letters are individual spans, so split any string), the three plate colours and the paper tint, and the two small caption strings. Keep the expo.out plate entries, the 0.05s letter stagger and the ghost offset amounts; reduce grain opacity for cleaner output.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the discs, the .k and .ghost word stacks split into .l spans, captions, the inline SVG filter and the .grain div; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the same tweens at fractions of D (plates 0-0.3D, letters 0.12D, exit 0.82D). Give the SVG filter id a per-instance suffix so two shots do not collide; selectors scoped to el.
caveats: feTurbulence grain over the full frame plus multiply blending is slow to render
mix-blend-mode needs isolation on the container to match the lab
